Cross-sectional momentum on US equities: a small-sample study.

Authors: Jane Doe, John Smith, Alex Reyes.

Abstract.

This paper studies cross-sectional momentum on the S&P 500 over the
sample period 2005-2020. We rebalance monthly and assume frictionless
trading (p.2). The strategy is a simple long-short basket built from
12-month total returns, skipping the most recent month.

Headline result.

The strategy delivers an annualised return of 11.5% with a Sharpe ratio
of 1.20 over the full sample period 2005-2020 (p.4). All numbers are
reported net of transaction costs estimated at 5 bps per trade.

Out-of-sample evaluation.

We split the sample into in-sample (2005-2014) and out-of-sample
(2015-2020) windows. The out-of-sample Sharpe ratio is 0.95, with a
maximum drawdown of 18.0% (p.7). Survivorship bias is addressed by
using a point-in-time S&P 500 universe.

Limitations.

The sample is regime-dependent and the strategy may underperform in
high-correlation regimes. Replication code is available at
https://github.com/example/momentum-replication so other researchers
can reproduce the results net of transaction costs. The strategy hit
rate is 56.0% across monthly trades.

Disclaimer.

Past performance does not guarantee future results.
